  I.  Roll Call
  A meeting of the Parking and Traffic Commission was held at City of Inglewood’s Community Room
  located on the 1st Floor on March 27, 2019 at 7pm. Commissioners and City Staff were present with the
  exception of Lieutenant James Kirk or Cardell Hurt.

 II.  Approval of Minutes for February 27, 2019
   Motion to accept the meeting notes was made by Commissioner Garcia
   Seconded by Commissioner Braggs
   Commissioner Brooks abstained the approval of the meeting notes
   Commissioner Roberts was not present for the voting.
   3-0 approved Meeting Minutes

III.  Public Comments (not listed on the agenda)
   Vehicles that did not move during street sweeping dates and times, residents can contact the Parking
  Enforcement. Parking Enforcement will notify and take responsibility for informing the street cleaning
  team to conduct a second round.
   Concrete found on sidewalks, potholes seen on the street and other public services, resident can contact
  Flynn Marine at (310) 412-5333 for assistance.
   Loud music or any disturbance in the neighborhood, residents should contact the police.
   Residents noted that homeless people are stationed on neighborhood streets and leave trash in the
  neighborhood area. Parking Enforcement needs to be informed of such vehicle to monitor even after
  the vehicle is moved.
   Crenshaw Service Road is a one-way street. Drivers are not alert and drive in the opposite direction.
  This is an enforcement issue and Police should be notified to monitor the matter.

IV.  Unfinished Business
   None

 V.  New Business

  Page 1 of 2
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION
 March 27, 2019 Meeting Minutes
    Residents are requesting the formation of a residential permit parking district on 11th Avenue between
  99th Street and Hardy Street due to the excessive number of cars parking on this street. Public Work
  expanded the areas 10th, 11th Ave and west of Crenshaw Service Road between Arbor Vitae St and
  99th Street and Hardy Street, 99th Street between 11th Avenue and west of Crenshaw Service Road to
  minimize spillage of the parking problem to adjacent residential streets to avoid any spillover effect.
  The requested permit parking hours are twenty-four hours a day seven days a week.
    Engineering report was read and explained by the City Traffic Engineer to the public of the data
  findings, which showed that there is not a parking issue in this area.
    The Commission allowed the residents who attended the meeting to come forward and provide public
  comments on the matter.
    After review of the study and hearing public comments, the Parking and Traffic Commissions voted to
  deny District 5-0 parking permit.
